2.  23-24829  Recommendation to receive and file all subcommittee updates.

  Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee Update
  • SubCommittee Chair Jim Howat provided the update.
  • The Annual Utility envelopes have been sent out and we hope to expect an
  increase in funds next month. The current objective is to raise funds and if

  4811 AIRPORT PLAZA DR.
  PACIFIC GATEWAY- ROSI ROOM, 3:30 PM

  anyone has any ideas or connections, please share them with the
  subcommittee.
  • Chair Julie Lie, asked that the staff look into having City of Long Beach staff
  donate to the Mayor’s Fund directly through their paystub. It had previously
  been done and it could be a good way to increase contributions.
  • Stephanie Sosa, Community Program Specialist added that a press release
  is expected to be released in November to highlight the season of giving.
  There is also a live stream with Mayor’s Fund recipient GP Blankets of Love
  that includes the mayor where they discuss the fund and all the positive work
  it can support.

  Policy Subcommittee Update
  • Subcommittee Chair provided the update.
  • The subcommittee met on Monday Oct 16, to continue to go over the Safe
  Sleep Program and how they can campaign for a pilot program here in Long
  Beach to Council.
  • Metro Transit homeless services programming was discussed. Metro has
  24/7 outreach teams on three metro lines, none of which are in Long Beach,
  they have a mobile unit that goes to the end of the line every night, and 25
  reserved interim beds for metro outreach. Metro is working with the County
  to get recognized as an encampment to free up funds and services to their
  stations.
  • The subcommittee will be making policy recommendations to the City
  Council in the upcoming months.

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Rew, seconded by Member Howat, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Lie, Rew, Johnson, Bedy, Howat, Chotiswatdi, Sngiem, Morquecho
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None

3.  23-24830  Recommendation to receive and file the presentation on Safe Sleep Sites from the
  City of Eugene, Oregon.

  Peter Chavannes, Homeless Systems Policy Manager from the City of Eugene,
  Oregon provided a verbal presentation via Zoom.
  He provided a brief overview of the Homeless programming available within
  jurisdiction, this includes the Safe Sleep sites, Rest Stop Program and more.
  • The City of Eugene required that these sites be distributed around the city to
  ensure that the PEH that were asked to move, would have a location to
  relocate to.

  Page 2 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 1, 2023
  4811 AIRPORT PLAZA DR.
  PACIFIC GATEWAY- ROSI ROOM, 3:30 PM

  • The first step was to look for land that could accommodate safe sleep sites.
  They used GIS software to create maps of available properties that met the
  criteria that included being close to food, homeless services, and public
  transportation. As well as hired a real estate broker and property acquisition
  manager.
  • Second, they started community engagement and took a more assertive but
  informative approach that shared clear measurements of success. The
  strategy included speaking with key stakeholders like Neighborhood
  Associations, door-to-door canvassing, and mass mailers.
  • Five sleep sites were created, these sites could shelter 40-60 people. Two of
  those sites were located on city-owned property, one is owned by the local
  transportation district and two are privately owned. Of the two privately
  owned sites had previously been identified as an affordable housing project
  that would be leased at a good rate of return, the other was much more
  costly.
  • The Rest Stop program, which holds about 20 people or less, also differs
  from the safe sleep sites since they are not low barrier programs. The Rest
  Step Program is a small non-congregate “Tiny home/Conestoga” shelters
  with no electricity. To gain access to the communities, PEH must complete
  an application, check-in with the provider on a weekly basis, cannot do drugs
  onsite but do not have to be clean and must listen to the facilitation team to
  ensure they are following the rules of the community.
  • Since these sites are not considered “shelter” using HUD’s standards,
  outreach is funded though navigation money. Funding these sites are all
  through one-time dollars, initially through the CAREs Act, then the American
  Rescue Funds and most recently, from the state that will get them through
  the fiscal year 2025.
  • The total annual cost for operations is 4.2 million, not including startup cost.
  • Members had questions regarding best practices and data sharing,
  behavioral health issues, and clarification on logistics for each program.
  • Peter answered.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Voting Member Bedy, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Johnson, Morquecho, Sngiem, Rew, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Simmons

5.  23-24832  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Proclamation Update.

  Stephanie Sosa, Community Program Specialist, presented.
  • The update provided will be given to Council.
  • Senator Gonzalez awarded the city $1.25 million to help seniors on the brink
  of homelessness and an additional $750.000 awarded for re-entry programs.
  • The tenant and landlord resources on the Community Development
  webpage have been updated.
  • Staff are collaborating with Pasadena Health Department on an advocacy
  strategy to allow for direct resources to local city health jurisdictions for
  mental health services.
  • The staff is also working with LAHSA around creating additional winter
  shelter beds at 702 as well as support with inclement weather beds. As well
  as engaging Los Angeles County DMH around timeline for reconvening co-
  located staffing at the MSC.
  • Community Outreach and Engagement recently had an educational virtual
  tiny home meeting to discuss the Tiny Homes program.
  • Staff are working with its community champions, to identify inclement
  weather sheltering locations in preparation for the cold, wet months to come.
  • Three affordable housing projects that include supportive housing units for
  PEH are in the process of having people matched to units, Lease ups for
  those matches will begin within the coming month at
  • Heritage Gardens
  • Wellspring-Participants have been matched.
  • 26.2- Applications are being completed

  search for available properties for projects. Using current funds to create a

6.  23-24833  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff Report.

  Jeffrey Proctor, Homeless Services Admin and Operations Officer, presented.
  • Outreach direct phone number, 562-470-4672(4MSC) is live and taking calls.
  o 476 requests for Outreach
  o 217 newly enrolled people in outreach
  o 483 outreach services provided.
  o 397 first-time visitors to the MSC
  o 3,089 total visits in September
  o 154 average daily visits
  o 172 Mobile Access Enrollments
  o 252 Mobile Access Center Services Provided
  • For the staffing update
  o Lauren Feiring has been transferred to a Public Health Professional III
  o 3 positions have been filled and will start in the month of November.
  o 5 positions currently in the recruitment/interview process
  o 6 positions that will begin soon.
  • The Safe Parking program was successfully relocated on Oct 23rd, the site
  is on Anaheim and Santa Fe, this program will be at the location for at least a
  year and has capacity for 50 vehicles.
  • Staffing for the mobile therapy program has been completed, project is
  anticipated to launch in December.
  • Staff continue to participate in the working group to create a HHAP 5
  regional plan for the Los Angeles County.
  • Two new locations were added to the MAC schedule in November.
  • Entering second phase with Bit Focus incorporating our CES data process
  into the HMIS platform
  • The Emergency Shelter at 702 Anaheim has added additional beds to
  support the winter months.
